templates.who: Employer: head of HR (CHRO, chief people officer)

subjects: How many of {{company_poss}} {{employees}} will land?
{{company}}: {{employees}} people, one search at once
templates.preview: Logins are easy to report. Landed is the number that matters.
templates.body:
{{first_name}},

Your outplacement vendor will report how many of the {{employees}} people leaving {{company}} logged in. Few will report how many landed. {{line_timing}}

That gap is the problem. Our monthly report on white-collar unemployment (Census and BLS data, methods published) shows 28% of unemployed white-collar workers still searching after 27 weeks, up from 23% a year ago. Most packages end at 90 days.

That's why I founded NextChapter, the leading job transition platform. Each affected person gets a search strategy, a pivot plan built from their work history, tailored jobs and a network to support them. That includes retraining for the gaps, networking outreach drafted for them, coaching, and exclusive jobs and recruiters. {{line_open_roles}} You get the number that matters: how many engaged, interviewed and landed, as counts, never names.

It works beside your vendor or replaces it. Is this yours, or should I send the one-pager to whoever owns the transition?
templates.fu1: {{first_name}}, one concrete thing I can send: the three-sentence note your team would paste to the {{employees}} affected employees, with the link already in it. Want it?
templates.fu2: {{first_name}}, I'll stop here so I don't clutter your inbox. If the timing changes, the offer stands: a pilot for the people leaving {{company}}.
templates.subject_fallback: {{employees}} jobs: the market its people face

templates.preview: 39% of claimants used up their benefits. Aggregate counts back to you.
templates.body:
{{first_name}},

Nationally, 39% of unemployment claimants used up their benefits in the 12 months to August, after drawing them for 15.8 weeks on average (Labor Department). Our monthly report on white-collar unemployment (Census and BLS data, methods published) shows 28% of unemployed white-collar workers still searching after 27 weeks, up from 23% a year ago. {{state}} employers filed notices for {{state_jobs_90d}} jobs in the last 90 days.

I built NextChapter, the leading job transition platform, for the claimants who outlast their benefits. Each person gets a search strategy, a pivot plan built from their work history, tailored jobs and a network to support them. That includes retraining for the gaps, networking outreach drafted for them, coaching, and exclusive jobs and recruiters. {{line_open_roles}} It is free to claimants and could sit alongside reemployment services and RESEA, with aggregate counts reported back.

May I send a two-paragraph summary and a demo built from {{state_poss}} own data?
templates.fu1: {{first_name}}, the summary is two paragraphs and the demo opens in one click. Which would be easier?
templates.fu2: {{first_name}}, I'll step back. If a colleague owns reemployment tools, a forward would be appreciated.

A layer beside your program
templates.preview: A test on one engagement. You keep the client.
templates.body:
{{first_name}},

Laid-off white-collar workers face about one opening per unemployed person (1.01 in August, BLS), and 27% of the unemployed have been out of work 27 weeks or more. Program end dates matter.

NextChapter is a layer beside your program: local job listings (our crawler tracks about 188,000 open white-collar roles), a skills-gap plan and AI training, and each person keeps a free account afterward. I would like to test it on one upcoming engagement; you keep the client.

Open to a 15-minute call?
templates.fu1: {{first_name}}, I can send a one-page summary of what your clients would see. Should I?
templates.fu2: {{first_name}}, I'll step back. If a client asks about local jobs or AI training, reply and I'll set up a test.
templates.ps: P.S. Figures come from our monthly white-collar employment report (BLS, JOLTS and Labor Department data, methods published). Layoff totals are from state WARN filings and role counts from our own job crawler.

templates.who: Researcher or policy analyst (AI displacement, unemployment, white-collar work)
templates.why: Credibility through method: leads with a finding they can check and asks for review, not a sale.
subjects: Data on white-collar layoffs and AI in filings
A method to review: AI in restructuring filings
templates.preview: Open methods and data files. A one-line reply is enough.
templates.body:
{{first_name}},

We publish a monthly white-collar employment report from public data, with methods and data files open. The September edition counted AI in restructuring filings: 16 of 170 this year (9.4%) cite it in the restructuring disclosure itself, and announced cuts cite it about 21% of the time. It also finds about one opening per unemployed person (1.01 in August).

{{line_researcher_hook}} May I send the report and the data files? A one-line reply is enough.
templates.fu1: {{first_name}}, the data files are small and the method is two pages. Shall I send them?
templates.fu2: {{first_name}}, I'll leave it there. If a figure ever looks wrong to you, I would want to hear it.
templates.ps: P.S. The report counts what filings say and does not claim AI caused a layoff.
templates.subject_fallback: Data on white-collar layoffs and AI in filings
